clue.text: Subordinate entertains at home as a way of drawing attention

indicators.note: to entertain is to have guests inside, so the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: an underling is a subordinate
at home means in

explanation.surface: A junior employee hosts guests at their house to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Underscoring words on a page is a common method of emphasising them.

clue.text: Where to keep one's voice down?

definitions.text: Where to keep one's voice down?

parts.words: Where to keep one's voice down?
parts.note: a whisper is said to be kept below the level of a breath, so the clue asks for the place a hushed voice goes

explanation.definitionFit: Speaking very quietly is idiomatically described as murmuring beneath the breath.

clue.text: When order is reversed to produce a low hum

indicators.note: is reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
to produce means the letters are brought out from within the words before them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions say to hum low whenever the sequence is flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no word signalling the hidden run; 'to produce' does that job, leaving the noun 'a low hum' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a continuous low monotonous sound, as of bees or bagpipes.

clue.text: A so-called German teacher comes up with an Italian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Otto is a stock German man's name
sir is a schoolchild's word for a male teacher

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed the German schoolmaster arrives bringing an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses OTTOSIR to give RIS + OTTO; Otto is a palindrome, so only SIR visibly turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Take over from a stylish woman with oomph

parts.note: in means fashionable
her refers to a woman
it means sex appeal, as in an It girl

explanation.surface: Someone replaces a fashionable, glamorous lady in her post.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit something is to succeed to it after another, taking it over from them.

clue.text: Irish king, sort of titan — pesky thing!

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: a sort of titan is a version of it with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish monarch, a giant of sorts, proves a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges TITAN to ITANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that annoys, an aggravating presence.

clue.text: Recreates hunger when drunk after a good meal?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Downing something after dinner brings appetite back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' scrambles RECREATES HUNGER; the definition is a playful description of when the liqueur is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Chartreuse is a herbal liqueur typically sipped as a digestif following dinner.

clue.text: Shells expressing disappointment

definitions.meaning: removes husks or pods, as with oysters or corn
a mild exclamation of regret or embarrassment

explanation.definitionFit: Shuck is a verb for stripping husks, and the plural form is a folksy exclamation of dismay.

clue.text: Joins up with enthusiasm at first — and respect

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of enthusiasm
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: meets means joins

explanation.surface: Someone joins in eagerly at the start and earns regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joins up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning enlists, but 'up' is a down-clue reversal signal; 'at first' places the E ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, a synonym of respect as a noun.

clue.text: Frightful to conceal duck when going to America

parts.note: hide means conceal
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
US is America

explanation.surface: Scary instruction to hide a waterfowl when travelling to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a zero score, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means dreadful or repulsive, so frightful in appearance.

clue.text: Three quarters go after tough firms

indicators.note: go after places the quarters behind the word for tough

parts.note: hard means tough
E, N and S are three of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Seventy-five percent of the money chases difficult companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firms' looks like a plural noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To firm something up is to make it solid, the sense of setting or stiffening.

clue.text: Blimey, Vicar, we've got a fixer here!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like blimey
a rector is a parish clergyman, like a vicar

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a clergyman has turned up to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrector is someone who puts errors right, one who mends things.

clue.text: Uptight at half score for the Home Counties

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half is ten
the Home Counties are the counties round London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about scoring half marks in the region near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense describes someone anxious and strained, a near synonym.

clue.text: Transported by the said smell

indicators.note: the said means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Someone is carried away by a particular fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent can mean thrilled or carried away in rapture, as in being transported.

clue.text: City in which thin man got lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A slender man went missing somewhere in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges THIN MAN GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is an English city in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Larva found some distance west on the Golden Mile

parts.note: an inch is a small distance
W is west
or is the heraldic word for gold
M is mile

explanation.surface: A caterpillar is discovered a little way along a seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry. The Golden Mile is the seafront at Blackpool, a British resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An inchworm is the caterpillar of a geometer moth, so an insect larva.

clue.text: Tatty tinsel, hard to free from enchantment

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and frayed, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Shabby Christmas decorations are tough to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tatty' rearranges TINSEL HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To disenthral is to release from bondage or a spell, liberating someone.

clue.text: Having a record in tax, becomes second-in-command

indicators.note: in places the record inside the word for tax

parts.note: a duty is a tax
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone with a criminal record in tax affairs gets promoted to number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a criminal past; it is an EP disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is an assistant who acts for the chief, ranking just below them.

clue.text: Eh? Ben's a confused old-timer

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of Ben's taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled elderly man named Ben says 'eh?'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges EH BENS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone past their prime, an old-timer whose day is over.

clue.text: Utterances ascribed to Jesus by silver artist, perhaps, without hesitation or afterthought

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: without means the named pieces are taken away from perhaps

parts.note: er is a hesitant noise
PS, a postscript, is an afterthought

explanation.surface: Sayings of Christ captured by a painter, perhaps, delivered without pause or addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like a hedge on 'artist', but is the word itself: remove ER and PS to leave PHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrapha are sayings attributed to Jesus that are not recorded in the canonical gospels.

clue.text: Murdoch may be a knight on retirement

parts.note: I is one, a

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title

explanation.surface: A newspaper tycoon might be knighted when he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Rupert Murdoch; it is the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was the Irish-born British novelist, so her first name fits.

clue.text: Sweden still wobbling at the end of the day

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
a jelly still wobbling has not set

explanation.surface: Sweden continues to sway as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset is when the sun goes down, the close of daylight.

clue.text: Take a rest from fish

definitions.meaning: to settle or sit briefly, as a bird does on a branch
a freshwater fish with spiny fins

explanation.definitionFit: Perch is both a verb for sitting briefly on a high place and the name of a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Sunday critic's review starts: "One appearing in Pinafore is due for the melting pot"

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the two words
appearing in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a pinafore is an apron
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Sunday paper reviewer opens a write-up of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta with a damning verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, but here pinafore is just an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap iron is waste metal collected to be melted down and recycled.

clue.text: For starters, people invited loved Agatha's unusual food

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Guests at a party adored Agatha's exotic cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like part of the definition but gives the final U.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice dish, an item of food.

clue.text: Got up after something to drink for growth

indicators.note: after places the word for got up behind the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink
rose means got up

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed after a cuppa for a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a type of rose bush, a plant that grows.

clue.text: Make harmful cutback with old instrument

parts.note: the single word splits as lop, meaning prune, followed by back, telling us to read lop in reverse
a lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Budget cuts and an antique instrument cause damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' is read as cut (LOP) back, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pollute is to contaminate, making air or water harmful.

clue.text: To buzz girl at the river is characteristic of people

parts.note: hum means buzz
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone hums at a girl by the riverside, as anyone would.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Human nature is the set of traits typical of mankind.
